lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.unitTitle: PF3 — Budgeting and Saving: Running the Adult Budget
lessonRef.title: Comparison and analysis: year-end reconciliation and lessons

objective: Compare a fictional household’s planned and actual savings rates across a year in which income rose, and establish where the additional income actually went.
scenario: The planned and actual year compared below belong to a fictional household. Every figure, including the simulated bonus, is invented for this exercise.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional annual plan and outturn in these directions

tasks.directions: The fictional household planned on take-home income of $46,800 for the year, spending of $42,600, and savings of $4,200. It actually took home $47,940, including a simulated bonus, spent $44,388, and saved $3,552.

prompts.text: What savings rate did the plan set, to two decimal places?
What savings rate did the year actually deliver, to two decimal places?
How much more income did the year bring than the plan assumed?

tasks.directions: Now trace where the extra income ended up.

prompts.text: How much more did the household spend than it planned?
By how much did savings fall short of the plan?
What proportion of the extra income did the additional spending come to, to two decimal places?
Did any part of the additional income reach savings?
choices: No — savings finished below plan despite the extra income

prompts.text: Income rose by $1,140.00 and savings fell by $648.00. Explain how a household can end a better-than-planned year with less saved than it planned, and name one change to how the plan handles unexpected income that would have produced a different result.

remediation: If the year looks like a success because income was $1,140.00 above plan, compare the savings rates rather than the income. The plan set 8.97% and the year delivered 7.41%. Then check where the extra went: spending rose $1,788.00, which is more than the extra income, and the difference came out of savings.
extension: Work out what the savings rate would have been had the household spent exactly its planned $42,600, and say how much of the improvement comes from the bonus rather than from any change in behaviour.
